Objective Know exactly what to do when a protocol you use is exploited, a stablecoin depegs, or your wallet is compromised.
Explanation — the 60-minute playbook 0–5 min: Verify.
Official channels only (bookmarked X/Discord/status page, security firms).
Don't click links in DMs, and don't sign anything "to protect funds".
Protocol exploit: withdraw if still possible and safe; revoke approvals to affected contracts.
exit below 0.99 for X hours); don't panic-sell far below it on a thin book.
Wallet compromise: move remaining assets to a fresh wallet (new seed, clean device); revoke approvals; assume the old seed is burned.
Check HFs across all positions (prices may be moving), top up from the reserve, and journal every action with timestamps.
What was the signal, what worked, and what changes in the caps and the register?

You verify on its bookmarked status page, see withdrawals still work on unaffected markets, withdraw your USDC, revoke the pool approval, check your other HFs, and journal it.

Check yourself. 1. First thing to do in an incident? The answer: Verify through official, bookmarked channels.
Check yourself. 2. Someone offers a link to "rescue your funds". What do you do? The answer: Ignore it. It's a common scam during incidents.
Check yourself. 3. Wallet compromised: can you keep using the seed? The answer: No. Move to a fresh wallet with a new seed; the old one is burned.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to know exactly what to do when a protocol you use is exploited, a stablecoin depegs, or your wallet is compromised.

Next, Depeg: follow your written peg rule (for example exit below 0.99 for X hours); don't panic-sell far below it on a thin book.
And finally, Wallet compromise: move remaining assets to a fresh wallet (new seed, clean device); revoke approvals; assume the old seed is burned.
